- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until sentiment improves.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply a 2–4% downward bias for first 5 days of forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from model (e.g., >5% error) and sentiment is mixed or negative, reduce forecast slope to match sentiment’s downward bias.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–3% downward correction starting from day 10–15 of forecast.
